ai_overview_note: Broad queries like 'why does AI invent fake personas' and 'why does ChatGPT make up information' trigger an AI Overview and a strong featured-snippet zone — these head terms are not winnable for a new domain. The specific first-person framing ('my own content agent invented a persona for a post about my work') has NO direct competing page and NO AI Overview, because it is a novel anecdote, not an answerable factual query.
featured_snippet_target: Definition-style block: 'Why do AI content agents invent fake author personas?' — 40-55 word answer (LLMs fill missing byline/author fields by pattern-completing plausible names + credentials unless the prompt/schema pins identity). This is the snippet most realistically contestable with a concrete first-person example.

outline.unique_angle: Every existing SERP result is journalism ABOUT publishers caught using fake AI bylines, or a victim of an external autonomous agent. None is a builder's first-person post-mortem of their OWN pipeline inventing a credentialed (nurse) persona on a post about the builder's own work — with the actual schema/prompt root cause traced and the concrete guard-rail fix shown. That self-inflicted, reproducible, code-level angle is the gap.

YMYL flag: the invented persona is a NURSE with a fake registration credential. Per project YMYL rules, the article must be explicit that the credential was fabricated by the pipeline and is not a real RN byline, or it risks the same E-E-A-T penalty it is describing.
